title: HarborPoint - Activation runway + technical intake
next_steps: Redwood to send 30-day activation plan deck by 2026-05-15
Customer to share network topology + firewall egress rules by 2026-05-20
SE to run initial throughput benchmark with 5k tokens/sample by 2026-05-22
action_items: Maya Lin: Email onboarding deck + pricing summary [due 2026-05-15]
Priya Nair: Schedule private infra intake and request VPN access for pilot team [due 2026-05-18]
Liam O'Connor: Provide VPC peering details and list of outbound IPs [due 2026-05-20]
Nadia Ruiz: Share SOC2 and encryption requirements doc and confirm KMS vendor [due 2026-05-19]
summary: Kickoff focused on first 30-day activation runway for HarborPoint's pilot of Redwood Dedicated. Covered roles, success criteria, technical intake (VPC, SSO, KMS, logging), timeline, and benchmarks. Agreement to run initial throughput/latency tests and exchange security docs.
transcript:
00:00 Maya Lin: Okay, hey everyone, this is Maya with Redwood, thanks for joining, we can do quick intros, um, we have about 50 minutes. 
00:08 Samira Gomez: Hi, Samira here, Head of Data at HarborPoint, Liam's on for platform, Nadia for security, Ethan for product. Thanks for hosting. 
00:16 Jonah Patel: Jonah CSM from Redwood, part of the playbook, I'll be running the activation tasks. 
00:22 Liam O'Connor: Liam, platform eng, we'll own the VPC and k8s side. 
00:28 Priya Nair: Priya SE, I'll lead the technical intake and benchmark. 
00:34 Ethan Park: Ethan, product, focusing on latency/cost targets for the chat flows. 
00:40 Maya Lin: Great, overview goal for today is to align on the 30-day activation runway, confirm success criteria, collect technical constraints and next steps. 
01:05 Samira Gomez: Our main goal is to validate throughput and make sure cost per request is predictable. We want to move from a POC to a limited production by end of quarter. 
01:20 Nadia Ruiz: Security: key points are SOC2 alignment, encryption at rest using our KMS, audit logs forwarded to our Splunk cluster, and data residency for EU customers. 
01:35 Maya Lin: Noted. For KMS we support BYOK with HSM integrations, and audit logs can be forwarded via syslog or SIEM connector, we have docs link in the deck. I'll share that. 
01:50 Priya Nair: Quick clarifying q about private vs dedicated: HarborPoint is planning on Dedicated reserved GPUs in our hosted cloud, is that right? Or are you leaning towards Private VPC? 
02:05 Liam O'Connor: We prefer Dedicated initially but with VPC peering so traffic never leaves our VPC, there might be a short list of customers that require full Private deployment. 
02:20 Maya Lin: Ok that hybrid approach is common — we can do Dedicated with customer-controlled egress and VPC peering; if later needed we can plan a Private rollout. 
02:35 Ethan Park: For success criteria, here's what matters to product: 95th percentile latency under 350ms for 512 token prompts, cost under $0.02 per generated token on average, and availability 99.9 during business hours. 
02:56 Jonah Patel: We'll document those as pilot KPIs. Some of those numbers may depend on model selection and quantization; SE follow up. 
03:12 Priya Nair: For benchmarking we'll run three profiles: 1) chat 512 tokens at steady 10 rps, 2) batch embeddings 128k rows, and 3) burst 50 rps to test autoscaling. 
03:32 Samira Gomez: Embeddings are critical for our recommender, so the batch window and throughput are important. 
03:40 Liam O'Connor: For network: we'll need Redwood outbound IPs, and we'll open egress to the dedicated pool; also we use strict egress via NAT and firewall rules. 
03:56 Maya Lin: We'll provide an IP list and a network checklist. Priya, can you own the intake template? 
04:05 Priya Nair: Yep, I'll share template after call. 
04:12 Nadia Ruiz: On compliance, we'll need proof of SOC2 and an export control check. Also SSO: we use Okta and require SAML with SCIM provisioning for role mappings. 
04:30 Priya Nair: Okta is supported; we can do SAML + SCIM for user provisioning. There's an interim step where we can grant console-only access scoped to namespaces until SCIM is fully provisioned. 
04:48 Ethan Park: Can we limit developer access to model logs? We don't want product internals exposed company-wide. 
04:55 Jonah Patel: Yes RBAC is granular, we can limit token viewing and redact sensitive fields. 
05:04 Maya Lin: I'll attach our 'security checklist' doc and the SAML guidance. 
05:12 Samira Gomez: Timeline — what are realistic milestones in the first 30 days? 
05:20 Maya Lin: Typical activation runway: week 1: intake+infra setup; week 2: pilot deploy and basic tests; week 3: run benchmarks and adjust configs; week 4: review, checklist, and handoff to ops. We can compress or expand depending on resource availability. 
05:45 Liam O'Connor: We can allocate 2 engineers for week 1-3, and product support for bench runs. 
05:53 Priya Nair: For benching I want sample prompt sets and embedding data schema. Samira can you share the CDR and a 1k prompt sample? 
06:05 Samira Gomez: Yes I'll drop a sanitized sample into the shared drive. 
06:12 Maya Lin: Great — regarding observability, Redwood Console has per-route token cost breakdown, latency histograms, and alerting; we'll grant Jonah monitoring access and create a dashboard for HarborPoint. 
06:28 Jonah Patel: We'll set up an alert for 95th percentile latency and cost-per-token threshold. 
06:35 Nadia Ruiz: Audit logs need to go to our Splunk; how long are they retained on Redwood side? 
06:42 Priya Nair: Default retention is 30 days in the console; we offer extended retention add-ons for compliance. We'll include options in pricing doc. 
06:55 Ethan Park: Any blockers we should call out? 
07:00 Liam O'Connor: Potential blocker is egress IP approvals from our networking team; might take a week. 
07:08 Maya Lin: We'll mark that as risk; provide IPs early. 
07:12 Priya Nair: On model selection: we recommend trying a quantized Llama-family variant for chat and a high-perf embedder for vectors; Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization levels. 
07:28 Samira Gomez: We do want to compare cost/quality tradeoffs — can Redwood run an eval across two model configs and produce a short report? 
07:36 Priya Nair: Yes SE team can run evals and share a comparison doc. 
07:42 Ethan Park: For the pilot scope, can we limit users to internal staff only, and then expand? 
07:49 Maya Lin: Absolutely — start internal only, then staged rollout. 
07:55 Jonah Patel: Next steps recap: Maya send deck + IP list by tomorrow; Priya send intake template; SE to schedule bench run; customer to share samples and network details. 
08:10 Samira Gomez: Sounds good. We'll put together a point-of-contact list. 
08:16 Nadia Ruiz: Also add a security POC for FedRAMP checks later. 
08:22 Maya Lin: Noted — we'll track as optional compliance runway. 
08:30 [link shared] https://redwood.ai/docs/activation-runway (may be transcribed variably) 
08:45 Priya Nair: Quick technical Q from Liam: what's the preferred kv cache warmup strategy for prefix caching — is it auto or manual? 
08:58 Priya Nair (cont): Redwood runtime supports both; for cold-starts we can populate KV cache via replayed sessions or synthetic warmup. I'll share procedure. 
09:10 Ethan Park: Regarding costs, how do we estimate burst pricing? 
09:17 Maya Lin: Burst capacity is charged as part of Dedicated and can be configured; we'll include an example pricing table for your expected 50 rps bursts. 
09:28 Liam O'Connor: Any known outages in past 6 months? We need SLA history. 
09:34 Jonah Patel: We publish uptime and incident history in the status page; plus Dedicated SLA is 99.9 with credits for breaches. We'll send incident summary. 
09:50 Samira Gomez: Ok, thanks all. Do we need to schedule a technical deep-dive? 
09:57 Priya Nair: I recommend a 90-min bench planning session next week with your engs. 
10:05 Samira Gomez: Let's do Tuesday 2026-05-19 10am ET. 
10:12 Maya Lin: I'll schedule and send invites. Thanks everyone. 
10:20 [Meeting ends]
